texts.Every chapter follows the same loop: goi: Every chapter follows the same loop: ごい (vocabulary), ぶんけい (sentence patterns), れいぶん (sample sentences), then れんしゅう (exercises). The workbook exercises come in six kinds: choosing the right grammar, rearranging words, filling in a passage, reading comprehension, question and answer, and translating English into Japanese.
texts.This is the most basic sentence in Japan: This is the most basic sentence in Japanese. It means "A is B", and the same pattern also covers "I am" and "they are". A and B are nouns or noun phrases. The marker は connects A and B and marks A as the topic, like "as for A". The ending です is the positive, polite copula, and it never changes for I, you, he, she or they. The particle は is written は but pronounced "わ".
texts.1.2 A wa B dewa arimasen / ja arimasen: 1.2 A は B では ありません / じゃ ありません
texts.To say \"A is not B\", change desu to de: To say "A is not B", change です to では ありません. Another way is じゃ ありません, where じゃ is the contracted form of では. Both are polite and mean the same thing. The word では is written では, and the は is read "わ".
texts.1.3 A wa B desu ka: 1.3 A は B です か
texts.To ask \"Is A B?\", put the question mar: To ask "Is A B?", put the question marker か at the end of the sentence. The word order does not change. The marker か works like a spoken question mark, so say the sentence with a rising tone.
texts.1.4 Hai and iie: answering a yes or no q: 1.4 はい and いいえ: answering a yes or no question
texts.The word hai means \"yes\" and iie means: The word はい means "yes" and いいえ means "no". Say はい with a positive sentence (A は B です) and いいえ with a negative one (A は B では ありません or じゃ ありません). In spoken Japanese the (A は) part is often dropped. If someone asks about "you" (あなた), answer about "I" (わたし).
texts.1.5 Hai, sou desu and iie, chigaimasu: 1.5 はい, そう です and いいえ、ちがいます
texts.These are two ready-made replies that sa: These are two ready-made replies that save you from repeating the whole sentence. The phrase はい、そうです means "Yes, that's right, I agree with you", and いいえ、ちがいます means "No, that's wrong, it's different". They work for any yes or no question.
texts.1.6 Iie, A wa C desu: 1.6 いいえ, A は C です
texts.In a negative answer, iie is normally pa: In a negative answer, いいえ is normally paired with the negative ending では ありません or じゃ ありません. When you also give the correct answer, the ending becomes positive です again, because you are now saying what is true. You can also say いいえ、ちがいます first and then add the right answer.
texts.A noun phrase is built by joining two or: A noun phrase is built by joining two or more nouns with a marker: noun の noun means "noun of noun" or "noun's noun", noun と noun means "noun and noun", and noun か noun means "noun or noun". The marker の is a modifier or possessive marker. It covers belonging (my office), relationship (the president of ADZ) and description (a Japanese language student). The main noun comes last, and you can stack more than one の in a row. A sentence can also end with の to mean "A's one", as in この くるまは アナさんのです.
texts.The marker to is an add-on marker meanin: The marker と is an add-on marker meaning "and". It joins nouns into a complete list: A and B, and nothing else. It only joins nouns, never whole sentences.
texts.The marker ka between two nouns means \": The marker か between two nouns means "or" and offers a choice. This is a different job from か at the end of a sentence, which makes a question. You can use both together to ask a choice question.
texts.The pattern C mo B desu means \"C is als: The pattern C も B です means "C is also B". The marker は changes to も and takes over its topic job, so you never use は and も on the same noun.
texts.1.11 A mo B desu ka: 1.11 A も B です か
texts.To ask \"Is A also B?\", use mo in the q: To ask "Is A also B?", use も in the question. A yes answer keeps も (はい, A も B です). In a negative answer, も changes back to は (いいえ, A は B では ありません or じゃ ありません), because "also" is no longer true.
texts.1.12 kono, sono, ano + noun: 1.12 この, その, あの + noun
texts.Japanese has four sets of pointing words: Japanese has four sets of pointing words, and all of them follow the same こ, so, a, do system. The こ words are near the speaker, the so words are near the listener, the a words are far from both, and the do words are the question words. The first set is この, その and あの. They mean "this", "that" and "that over there", and they must always be followed by a noun. A sentence can end with の to mean "mine" or "John's", as in その カメラは わたしのです.
texts.1.13 kore, sore, are: 1.13 これ, それ, あれ
texts.The words kore, sore and are mean \"this: The words これ, それ and are mean "this one", "that one" and "that one over there". They stand alone with no noun after them, and they are used only for things, not for people or places. The same こ, so, a rule applies: これ is near the speaker, それ is near the listener, and are is far from both.
texts.1.14 koko, soko, asoko: 1.14 ここ, そこ, あそこ
texts.These words point to places: koko is \"h: These words point to places: ここ is "here", そこ is "there" near the listener, and あそこ is "over there". The place word can come first (ここ は X です) or last (X は ここ です).
texts.1.15 kochira, sochira, achira: 1.15 こちら, そちら, あちら
texts.These words point to directions: kochira: These words point to directions: こちら is "this way", そちら is "that way", and あちら is "that way over there". They are also the polite way to point to a place in formal conversation. The word こちら has one more job: it introduces a person, because これ would be rude for a person.
texts.1.16 A wa (question word) desu ka: 1.16 A は (question word) です か
texts.To ask about something you do not know,: To ask about something you do not know, put the question word where the answer would go. The sentence still ends with です か. The question words in this chapter are だれ and どなた (who), だれの and どなたの (whose), なん (what), なんの (what kind of), どれ (which one), どの + noun (which noun), どこ (where) and どちら (which way). The word なん changes to なに when a marker follows it.
texts.This, that and over there (ko, so, a): This, that and over there (こ, そ, あ)
texts.The marker wa means \"as for A\", and mo: The marker は means "as for A", and も means "A とお". Never put both on the same noun.
texts.In the question A mo B desu ka, a no ans: In the question A も B です か, a no answer changes も back to は: いいえ, A は B じゃ ありません。
texts.The particle wa is written は but read \": The particle は is written は but read "わ", and では is written では.
texts.dewa arimasen and ja arimasen: では ありません and じゃ ありません
texts.The two endings mean exactly the same th: The two endings mean exactly the same thing. じゃ is the short, casual form of では, and both stay polite.
texts.The ending desu is positive and dewa ari: The ending です is positive and では ありません is negative. Never say "です では ありません".
texts.ka at the end and ka in the middle: か at the end and か in the middle
texts.At the end of a sentence, ka makes a que: At the end of a sentence, か makes a question: にほんじんです か (Is he Japanese?).
texts.Between two nouns, ka means \"or\": niho: Between two nouns, か means "or": にほんじんか アメリカじん (Japanese or American).
texts.A choice question uses both: sensei wa o: A choice question uses both: せんせいは おんなですか、おとこですか.
texts.no, to and ka between nouns: の、と and か between nouns
texts.The marker no means A's B, to means A an: The marker の means A's B, と means A and B (a complete list), and か means A or B (a choice).
texts.With stacked nouns the main noun comes l: With stacked nouns the main noun comes last: にほんご の せんせい (Japanese teacher), アナさんの にほんごの せんせい (Ana's Japanese teacher).
texts.When no ends a sentence it means \"A's o: When no ends a sentence it means "A's one": この くるまは アナさんのです.
texts.The words kono, sono and ano need a noun: The words この, その and あの need a noun right after them: この ほん (this book).
texts.The words kore, sore and are stand alone: The words これ, それ and are stand alone as "this thing" or "that thing": これ は ほん です。
texts.Both sets are for things. For a person s: Both sets are for things. For a person say この かた or こちら, and for a place say ここ.
texts.The words sono, sore, soko and sochira a: The words その, それ, そこ and そちら are near the listener.
texts.The words ano, are, asoko and achira are: The words あの, are, あそこ and あちら are far from both of you.
texts.If the thing is near you, use kono, kore: If the thing is near you, use この, これ, ここ or こちら。
texts.The words koko, soko and asoko are place: The words ここ, そこ and あそこ are places: ここは わたしの へやです.
texts.The words kochira, sochira and achira ar: The words こちら, そちら and あちら are directions, and a politer way to point at a place.
texts.The word kochira also introduces a perso: The word こちら also introduces a person: こちらは きむらさんです. Never use これ for a person.
texts.The word dare is casual \"who\" and dona: The word だれ is casual "who" and どなた is the polite one. Add の for "whose": だれの, どなたの.
texts.Use donata for a teacher or someone you: Use どなた for a teacher or someone you do not know well.
texts.nan, nani and nanno: なん, なに and なんの
texts.The word nan means \"what\". It changes: The word なん means "what". It changes to なに when a marker follows it.
texts.The word nanno means \"what kind of\" an: The word なんの means "what kind of" and always sits in front of a noun: なんの かいしゃ (what kind of company).
texts.dore, dono, doko and dochira: どれ, どの, どこ and どちら
texts.The word dore stands alone and means \"w: The word どれ stands alone and means "which one" of several things.
texts.The word dono needs a noun after it: don: The word どの needs a noun after it: どの ほん (which book).
texts.The word doko is \"where\" and dochira i: The word どこ is "where" and どちら is "which way", and also a polite "where".
texts.Use chichi, haha, ani, ane, otouto, imou: Use ちち, はは, あに, あね, おとうと, いもうと, そふ and そぼ for your own family.
texts.Use otousan, okaasan, oniisan, oneesan,: Use おとうさん, おかあさん, おにいさん, おねえさん, おとうとさん, いもうとさん, おじいさん and おばあさん for someone else's family.
texts.The exception: you may call your own fat: The exception: you may call your own father and mother おとうさん and おかあさん when you speak to them.
texts.Never put san on your own family. Say ch: Never put さん on your own family. Say ちち, not ちち さん.
texts.shain, kaishain, hito and kata: しゃいん, かいしゃいん, ひと and かた
texts.A kaishain is a company employee. A shai: A かいしゃいん is a company employee. A しゃいん is an employee, often with the company name in front: ADZ の しゃいん。
texts.The words hito and kata both mean \"pers: The words ひと and かた both mean "person", and かた is the polite one: この かた (this person), その ひと (that person).
texts.Do not use anata with a boss or someone: Do not use あなた with a boss or someone you do not know well. Use their name plus さん.
texts.Put san after other people's names, neve: Put さん after other people's names, never after your own.
texts.Add jin for the people and go for the la: Add じん for the people and go for the language: にほん, にほんじん, にほんご。
texts.English is the exception: eigo, never am: English is the exception: えいご, never アメリカご.
texts.hai, sou desu and iie, chigaimasu: はい、そうです and いいえ、ちがいます
texts.The reply hai, sou desu means \"Yes, tha: The reply はい、そうです means "Yes, that's right". The reply いいえ、ちがいます means "No, that's wrong".
texts.A plain iie is followed by the negative: A plain いいえ is followed by the negative or by the right answer: いいえ, ぶちょう です。
texts.Long vowels are doubled in romaji: gakko: Long vowels are doubled in romaji: がっこう, せんせい, おとうさん. Length changes the word, so practice pairs such as とき, とうき and とっき。
texts.A small っ holds a short pause: hakkiri,: A small っ holds a short pause: はっきり, ほっぺた, もった, かった。
texts.A small ゃ, ゅ or ょ joins the sound before: A small ゃ, ゅ or ょ joins the sound before it: とうきょう, ぎゅうにゅう, みょうじ。
texts.The sounds i and u are often almost sile: The sounds い and う are often almost silent: です, ききます, りゅうがくせい, わかっています。
texts.The sound n before b, m or p is pronounc: Before b, m or p, the nasal sound ん can sound closer to m. Examples include しんぶん and かんぱい. Reveal romaji to compare the alternative spellings.
texts.The ng sound: tenki can sound like tengk: The nasal sound ん can change slightly with the sounds around it. Listen for the nasal sound in てんき and ありがとう. Reveal romaji to compare the phonetic spellings.

texts.2.1 A wa Location ni arimasu: 2.1 A は Location に あります
texts.This pattern says that a thing is in a p: This pattern says that a thing is in a place. The thing (A) is the topic, so it takes は. The marker に points to the place where it is, and あります means "is" or "exists" for non-living things. The focus of the sentence is where A is, and the listener usually already knows what A is. Place words can be a name (しんじゅく), a word like へや (room), or a pointing word like あそこ (over there).
My office is in しんじゅく.
My dormitory is in しぶや.
texts.2.2 A wa Location ni arimasen: 2.2 A は Location に ありません
texts.To say a thing is not in a place, change: To say a thing is not in a place, change あります to ありません. Everything else stays the same, including は and に。
texts.2.3 A wa Location ni arimasu ka: 2.3 A は Location に あります か
texts.To ask whether a thing is in a place, ad: To ask whether a thing is in a place, add か at the end of the sentence. To ask where something is, put どこ (where) in the place slot: どこ に あります か. The short reply そうですか means "Oh, I see" when you are told something new. It is different from はい、そうです ("Yes, that's right") from Chapter 1.
texts.Is your office in Shinjuku?: Is your office in しんじゅく?
texts.Is your company in Shibuya?: Is your company in しぶや?
texts.Is the office in Shibuya?: Is the office in しぶや?
texts.No, it is not in Shibuya. It is in Shinj: No, it is not in しぶや. It is in しんじゅく.
texts.2.4 A wa Location ni imasu: 2.4 A は Location に います
texts.This is the same shape as 2.1, but for p: This is the same shape as 2.1, but for people and animals. The verb います is the verb of existence for living things that move, and it is used even when you only talk about where someone is. The focus is the location of A.
texts.2.5 A wa Location ni imasen: 2.5 A は Location に いません
texts.To say a person or animal is not in a pl: To say a person or animal is not in a place, change います to いません.
texts.2.6 A wa Location ni imasu ka: 2.6 A は Location に います か
texts.To ask whether a person or animal is in: To ask whether a person or animal is in a place, add か to the います sentence. To ask where someone is, use どこ に います か. In a reply, も means "also": すずきさんも ドイツに います (Suzuki is in Germany too).
texts.A locative is a position word such as ue: A locative is a position word such as うえ (on top), した (under) or なか (inside). It tells the exact spot, not just the general place. Name the thing first, then no, then the position word: つくえの うえ (on top of the desk). The whole phrase works like any other place, so you can add に あります or に います after it. The word あいだ (between) needs two things joined by to: ほんやと ぎんこうの あいだ. The full list of position words is in the Vocabulary section.
texts.2.8 Location ni A ga arimasu: 2.8 Location に A が あります
texts.This is the second sentence shape, and i: This is the second sentence shape, and it has a different job. Instead of saying where a known thing is, it says that something exists in a place, so the place comes first. The marker が points at the thing that exists. Use あります for non-living things. The focus is the existence of A in that place, and A is usually new information for the listener.
texts.2.9 Location ni (wa) A ga arimasen: 2.9 Location に (は) A が ありません
texts.To say there is nothing in a place, chan: To say there is nothing in a place, change あります to ありません. You can add は after に (に は) to stress the place, as if you were saying "in this place, at least, there is none". The meaning stays the same.
texts.2.10 Location ni A ga arimasu ka: 2.10 Location に A が あります か
texts.To ask whether something exists in a pla: To ask whether something exists in a place, add か. To ask what is there, use なに が: へや の なか に なに が あります か. The word なん becomes なに before a marker such as が.
texts.2.11 Location ni A ga imasu: 2.11 Location に A が います
texts.This is the same shape as 2.8, but for p: This is the same shape as 2.8, but for people and animals. It says that someone or something living exists in a place. The verb います does not change for one or many, so "there is a dog" and "there are dogs" are both いぬ が います.
texts.2.12 Location ni (wa) A ga imasen: 2.12 Location に (は) A が いません
texts.To say there is nobody in a place, chang: To say there is nobody in a place, change います to いません. As in 2.9, you can add は after に for emphasis.
texts.2.13 Location ni A ga imasu ka: 2.13 Location に A が います か
texts.To ask whether someone is in a place, ad: To ask whether someone is in a place, add か. To ask where someone is, use the first shape instead (どこ に います か, as in 2.6). To ask who is there, use だれ が います か. That question is not in your workbook, but it works the same way as なに が あります か.
texts.arimasu and imasu: あります and います
texts.The verb arimasu is for things that do n: The verb あります is for things that do not move on their own: bags, keys, buildings, tables.
texts.The verb imasu is for people and animals: The verb います is for people and animals: アナ さん, いぬ, ねこ。
texts.Plants such as ki (tree) use arimasu, no: Plants such as き (tree) use あります, not います.
texts.Pick the verb by what exists, not by wha: Pick the verb by what exists, not by what the sentence is about. A person's location still takes います: アナさんは にほんに います.
texts.The negatives are arimasen and imasen, a: The negatives are ありません and いません, and the questions add か: あります か, います か。
texts.The shape A wa Location ni arimasu answe: The shape A は Location に あります answers "where is it?". The thing is already known, so it gets は.
texts.The shape Location ni A ga arimasu answe: The shape Location に A が あります answers "what is there?" or "is there one?". The place comes first and the new thing gets が.
texts.The same fact can use either shape: kiss: The same fact can use either shape: きっさてん は ほんや の となり に あります (where the coffee shop is) and ほんや の となり に きっさてん が あります (there is a coffee shop next to the bookstore).
texts.The marker ni points at the place where: The marker に points at the place where something is or exists.
texts.The marker wa goes after the thing you a: The marker は goes after the thing you are talking about in shape one. It does not go after the place.
texts.The marker ga goes after the thing that: The marker が goes after the thing that exists in shape two.
texts.The words ni wa after a place only add e: The words に は after a place only add emphasis in negative sentences: へやに(は) いすが ありません. The meaning stays the same.
texts.Use doko ni for \"where\": ginkou wa dok: Use どこ に for "where": ぎんこう は どこ に あります か。
texts.Use nani ga for \"what is there\": kaban: Use なに が for "what is there": かばんの なかに なにが ありますか.
texts.The word nan changes to nani before a ma: The word なん changes to なに before a marker such as が.
texts.The question words stay in the same slot: The question words stay in the same slot as the answer. A place goes in the どこ slot, and a thing goes in the なに slot.
texts.Say the thing first, then no, then the p: Say the thing first, then no, then the position word: つくえの うえ (on top of the desk), never うえ の つくえ.
texts.The word aida needs two things joined by: The word あいだ needs two things joined by to: ほんやと ぎんこうの あいだ.
texts.to say exactly where something is, the w: to say exactly where something is, the whole phrase goes before に: つくえの うえ に あります。
texts.tonari, soba, yoko, chikaku and mukou: となり, そば, よこ, ちかく and むこう
texts.The words tonari, soba and yoko all mean: The words となり, そば and よこ all mean "beside".
texts.The word chikaku means \"near\", so it i: The word ちかく means "near", so it is less exact than beside.
texts.The word mukou means \"across\" or \"on: The word むこう means "across" or "on the other side".
texts.The word hidari is left and migi is righ: The word ひだり is left and みぎ is right. A thing on the left or right of another thing is also beside it.
texts.The word ryou (dormitory) is not ryoushi: The word りょう (dormitory) is not りょうしん (parents).
texts.The words kissaten and kafe mean the sam: The words きっさてん and カフェ mean the same thing.
texts.The word denwa is a phone, and keitai (d: The word でんわ is a phone, and けいたい(でんわ) is a cell phone.
texts.The word kodomo is \"children\" or \"chi: The word こども is "children" or "child", and こ is the short form.
texts.The words ima (now) and imasu (there is): The words いま (now) and います (there is) look alike but are different words.
texts.sou desu ka and hai, sou desu: そうですか and はい、そうです
texts.The phrase hai, sou desu means \"Yes, th: The phrase はい、そうです means "Yes, that's right". You say it to confirm something.
texts.The phrase sou desu ka means \"Oh, I see: The phrase そうですか means "Oh, I see". You say it after you learn something new, with a rising tone.
texts.Long vowels are doubled in romaji: byoui: Long vowels are doubled in romaji: びょういん, こうじょう, としょかん, きょうしつ, りょう, りょうしん, かいぎしつ. Do not shorten them.
A small っ holds a short pause: きっさてん。

Japanese numbers are built like blocks. Once you know 0 to 10, you can make every number up to 99. Say the tens digit, then じゅう (ten), then the ones digit. So 11 is じゅういち (ten and one), 20 is にじゅう (two tens), 25 is にじゅうご (two tens and five) and 99 is きゅうじゅうきゅう. Numbers from 11 to 19 have nothing in front of じゅう: it is じゅういち, not いち じゅういち.
texts.Three numbers have two readings: 4 is yo: Three numbers have two readings: 4 is よん or し, 7 is なな or しち, and 9 is きゅう or く. Use よん, なな and きゅう as your safe default, because those are the ones the book uses in phone numbers and prices. The number 0 has three readings too: ゼロ, れい and まる. The word れい also means "example", and まる also means "circle".
texts.Hundreds work the same way: say the numb: Hundreds work the same way: say the number first, then ひゃく. So 200 is にひゃく and 500 is ごひゃく. On its own, ひゃく is 100, with no いち in front of it. Three hundreds change their sound, so learn them as special readings: 300 is さんびゃく, 600 is ろっぴゃく and 800 is はっぴゃく.
texts.To say a number like 684, keep going fro: To say a number like 684, keep going from left to right: ろっぴゃく (600), はちじゅう (80), よん (4).
Thousands follow the same idea with せん. 1,000 is せん, 2,000 is にせん and 5,000 is ごせん. Two thousands are special readings: 3,000 is さんぜん and 8,000 is はっせん.
texts.The word sen turns into issen when a big: The word せん turns into いっせん when a bigger number comes before it. That only matters from 11,000 up, as in いちまん いっせん (11,000). On its own, 1,000 is just せん. To say 9,713, go from left to right: きゅうせん (9,000), ななひゃく (700), じゅうさん (13).
texts.1,000 after a bigger number (ichi man is: 1,000 after a bigger number (いちまん いっせん is 11,000)
texts.Japanese counts in groups of four digits: Japanese counts in groups of four digits, not three. English has thousand and million, but Japanese has man (10,000) and おく (100,000,000). So 10,000 is いちまん (1 x 10,000), and you always say the いち. 100,000 is じゅうまん (ten ten-thousands), 1,000,000 is ひゃくまん (one hundred ten-thousands), 10,000,000 is せんまん and 100,000,000 is いちおく.
texts.To read a big number, cut it into four-d: To read a big number, cut it into four-digit groups from the right. For 1,500,000 the groups are 150 and 0000, so you say 150, then man: ひゃくごじゅうまん. For 11,500 the groups are 1 and 1500, so you say いちまん, then 1,500, and せん becomes いっせん: いちまんいっせんごひゃく.
texts.3.5 Prices: ikura desu ka: 3.5 Prices: いくら です か
texts.To ask a price, use ikura (how much): A: To ask a price, use いくら (how much): A は いくら です か. To ask for a rough price, add ぐらい (about): A は いくらぐらいですか. To answer, say the number and then the currency: えん (yen), ドル (dollars) or peso (pesos). So 180 yen is ひゃく はちじゅう えん.
texts.The phrase zenbu de means \"in total, fo: The phrase ぜんぶ で means "in total, for all of it together". It goes at the front of the sentence: ぜんぶで いくらですか. To check a price, say the amount and add か, like any yes or no question: さんびゃくごじゅうえんですか. The answer is はい、そうです (yes, that is right) or いいえ、ちがいます (no, that is not right) and then the real price.
texts.3.6 Phone numbers: denwa bangou wa nan d: 3.6 Phone numbers: でんわばんごうは なんですか
texts.To ask for a phone number, say denwa ban: To ask for a phone number, say でんわばんごうは なんですか (what is it?) or でんわばんごうは なんばんですか (what number is it?). For a cell phone, use けいたいばんごう. Both questions mean the same thing in everyday use.
texts.To say the number, read every digit on i: To say the number, read every digit on its own. Never group them like "eighty-four". Say の for the hyphen. A zero can be zero, れい or まる, so pick one and keep it. Use よん, なな and きゅう for 4, 7 and 9, as the book does. For example, 7326-5471 is なな さん に ろく の ご よん なな いち.
texts.In Japanese you do not just say \"three: In Japanese you do not just say "three apples". You add a counter, which is a short ending that depends on what you are counting. This chapter teaches つ (anything), さい (age), にん (people), まい (thin, flat things), ほん (long, thin things), さつ (books and notebooks), かい (times), かい (floors of a building), こ (small things), ひき (small animals), だい (machines and vehicles) and ban or ばんめ (order, such as which child you are). Pages use the counter ページ. The number and the counter join into one word: さん plus こ is さんこ.
texts.There are two ways to use a counter with: There are two ways to use a counter with a noun. You can say the noun and then the counter, as in りんご さんこ, or the counter, then no, then the noun, as in さんこの りんご. Both mean three apples.
texts.Some counters change their sound with ce: Some counters change their sound with certain numbers, mostly 1, 3, 6, 8 and 10 (いっぽん, さんぼん, ろっぽん, はっぽん, じゅっぽん). People have special readings for 1, 2 and 4 (ひとり, ふたり, よにん). The general counter つ has its own word for every number from 1 to 10. The table below shows 1 to 4 for every counter, and the Vocabulary section has the full list up to 10.
texts.1st to 4th in order or family (ban, banm: 1st to 4th in order or family (ばん, ばんめ)
texts.Counters fit into the sentences you alre: Counters fit into the sentences you already know. With です, the sentence says what the count is: A は counter です, as in おとうとは はたちです (my younger brother is 20). With います or あります, it says how many there are in a place: Location に A が counter います (or あります), as in きょうしつに がくせいが じゅうごにん います.
texts.In the second shape, the counter sits ri: In the second shape, the counter sits right in front of the verb, after the thing and its が. Use います for people and animals, and あります for things. On this page the number and counter are written as one word (じゅうごにん, さんびゃくにん, さんじゅうごさい). When a number runs into the hundreds and has more digits after them, the hundreds stay a separate word: にひゃく ななじゅうにん (270 people).
texts.To ask how many, put nan in front of the: To ask how many, put なん in front of the counter: なんにん (how many people), なんぼん (long things), なんさつ (books), なんびき (small animals), なんだい (machines and vehicles), なんまい (flat things), なんこ (small things), なんかい (how many times), なんがい (what floor) and なんばんめ (which number in a family or line). For things counted with つ, and for age, use いくつ (how many things) and おいくつ (how old, polite). The word なんさい also asks for age.
texts.Use these question words in the same two: Use these question words in the same two shapes as the last lesson: A は question word です か, and Location に A が question word あります か (things) or います か (people and animals). Before a counter it is なん, never なに.

texts.A zero can be zero, rei or maru. All thr: A zero can be zero, れい or まる. All three are fine, so pick one.

texts.Sankai and sangai: さんかい and さんがい
texts.The ending kai is written the same for t: The ending かい is written the same for times and floors, but the sound for 3 differs: 3 times is さんかい and the 3rd floor is さんがい.
texts.For 1, 6, 8 and 10 the two meanings soun: For 1, 6, 8 and 10 the two meanings sound the same: いっかい, ろっかい, はちかい or はっかい, and じゅっかい. The sentence tells you which one is meant.
texts.The question words differ too: nankai as: The question words differ too: なんかい asks how many times, and なんがい asks what floor.
texts.People take nin. Small animals take hiki: People take にん. Small animals take ひき. Machines and vehicles take だい. Books and notebooks take さつ.
texts.Thin, flat things take mai, for example: Thin, flat things take まい, for example paper, tickets, stamps and letters.
texts.Long, thin things take hon, for example: Long, thin things take ほん, for example pencils, pens, bottles and umbrellas.
texts.Small things take ko, for example apples: Small things take こ, for example apples and oranges.
texts.When you are unsure, the general counter: When you are unsure, the general counter つ works for many things, up to 10.
texts.Age takes sai. Floors and times both tak: Age takes さい. Floors and times both take かい. Order or rank in a family takes ban or ばんめ。
texts.The counters shift mostly on 1, 3, 6, 8: The counters shift mostly on 1, 3, 6, 8 and 10. With ほん: いっぽん, さんぼん, ろっぽん, はっぽん, じゅっぽん. With ひき: いっぴき, さんびき, ろっぴき, はっぴき, じゅっぴき。
texts.With ko the changes are ikko, rokko, hak: With こ the changes are いっこ, ろっこ, はっこ and じゅっこ, but さんこ stays plain.
texts.With satsu the changes are issatsu, hass: With さつ the changes are いっさつ, はっさつ and じゅっさつ. The rest are plain.
texts.The numbers 2, 4, 5, 7 and 9 stay plain:: The numbers 2, 4, 5, 7 and 9 stay plain: にほん, よんほん, ごほん, ななほん, きゅうほん。
texts.People are special on 1, 2 and 4 only: h: People are special on 1, 2 and 4 only: ひとり, ふたり, よにん. After that they are plain: さんにん, ごにん, ろくにん。
texts.Ikura, ikutsu and nan plus a counter: いくら, いくつ and なん plus a counter
texts.ikura asks about a price. ikutsu asks ho: いくら asks about a price. いくつ asks how many things. なん plus a counter asks how many of one kind: なんにん, なんびき, なんだい。
texts.For age, oikutsu is the polite question: For age, おいくつ is the polite question and なんさい is also fine.
Before a counter it is なん, never なに. Say なんにん, not なににん.
texts.ikura gurai asks for a rough price. The: いくら ぐらい asks for a rough price. The word ぐらい means about.
texts.Noun then counter: ringo sanko. Counter,: Noun then counter: りんご さんこ. Counter, no, then noun: さんこの りんご. Both mean three apples.
texts.In the sentence shape Location ni A ga c: In the sentence shape Location に A が counter います, the counter sits between が and the verb: がくせい が ふたり います。
texts.Imasu or arimasu with counters: います or あります with counters
texts.People and animals take imasu: gakusei g: People and animals take います: がくせい が ふたり います, いぬ が さんびき います。
texts.Things take arimasu: ringo ga itsutsu ar: Things take あります: りんご が いつつ あります。
texts.The verb does not change with the number: The verb does not change with the number. います stays います for one dog or ten.
texts.Age 20 has its own special word, hatachi: Age 20 has its own special word, はたち. Learn it as a separate word.
texts.Ages 1, 8 and 10 shift their sound: issa: Ages 1, 8 and 10 shift their sound: いっさい, はっさい and じゅっさい。
texts.Other ages are the number plus sai, for: Other ages are the number plus さい, for example さんじゅうごさい (35)。 おいくつ and なんさい ask the question.
texts.Say the amount first, then the currency:: Say the amount first, then the currency: せん えん, ごひゃく ドル, いちまん ペソ。
texts.The book writes doru as do-ru in one exa: The book writes ドル as ドール in one example, but the word is ドル.
texts.Check a price with the amount and ka: sa: Check a price with the amount and か: さんびゃくごじゅうえんですか. Reply with はい、そうです or いいえ、ちがいます.
texts.Write each number in romaji. For example: Write each number in romaji. For example, 64 is ろくじゅう よん.
Write each number in romaji. For example, 684 is ろっぴゃくはちじゅうよん.
Write each number in romaji. For example, 9,713 is きゅうせんななひゃくじゅうさん.
Write each number in romaji. For example, 11,657 is いちまんいっせんろっぴゃくごじゅうなな.
texts.Write each price in romaji with the curr: Write each price in romaji with the currency after the number. For example, ¥5,360 is ごせん さんびゃく ろくじゅう えん.
texts.Write each phone number in romaji, one d: Write each phone number in romaji, one digit at a time. For example, 8254-3762 is はち に go よん の さん なな ろく に.
texts.Make a sentence in the shape A no denwa: Make a sentence in the shape A no でんわばんごう は (number) です. For example, かいしゃ 7636-5672 becomes かいしゃ の でんわばんごう は なな ろく さん ろく の go ろく なな に です.

texts.To say the hour, put the number in front: To say the hour, put the number in front of じ (o'clock): さんじ is 3 o'clock and じゅうにじ is 12 o'clock. Three hours have special readings that you have to learn by heart: 4 o'clock is よじ (never よんじ), 7 o'clock is しちじ (never ななじ) and 9 o'clock is くじ (never きゅうじ). To ask the hour, say なんじ (what time).
texts.For minutes, put the number in front of: For minutes, put the number in front of fun or ぷん. The ending changes with the number. The numbers 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 take ぷん, and 1, 6, 8 and 10 also squeeze the sound before it: いっぷん, さんぷん, よんぷん, ろっぷん, はっぷん, じゅっぷん. The numbers 2, 5, 7 and 9 take fun: にふん, ごふん, ななふん, きゅうふん. Bigger numbers follow their last digit, so 15 is じゅうごふん, 30 is さんじゅっぷん and 45 is よんじゅうごふん. To ask for minutes, say なんぷん (what minute).
texts.When you say a full time, the big part c: When you say a full time, the big part comes first, so the hour goes before the minutes: いちじ じゅうごふん is 1:15. The word はん (half) is a shortcut for 30 minutes: じゅうにじ はん is 12:30. For a.m. and p.m., put ごぜん (a.m.) or ごご (p.m.) in front of the time: ごぜん くじ is 9 a.m. and ごご しちじ is 7 p.m.
texts.Every day of the week ends in youbi (day: Every day of the week ends in ようび (day of the week). The first part is the name of the sun, the moon and five elements, which helps you remember them: にち (sun), げつ (moon), か (fire), すい (water), もく (wood), きん (gold) and do (earth). So にちようび is Sunday (sun day) and きんようび is Friday (gold day). The book lists the week starting on Sunday.
texts.To ask which day it is, use nanyoubi (wh: To ask which day it is, use なんようび (what day of the week). The word なんようび follows the same なん plus ending idea you saw with なんじ and なんぷん。
texts.A month is the number plus gatsu: ichiga: A month is the number plus がつ: いちがつ is January, さんがつ is March and じゅうにがつ is December. Three months have special readings, so do not use the plain numbers: April is しがつ (not よんがつ), July is しちがつ (not なながつ) and September is くがつ (not きゅうがつ). Ask with なんがつ (what month).
texts.The ending gatsu names a month on the ca: The ending がつ names a month on the calendar, such as March. It is not the word for counting how many months pass, which comes in Chapter 5.
texts.4.4 Days of the month: nichi: 4.4 Days of the month: にち
texts.A day of the month is the number plus ni: A day of the month is the number plus にち, but the first ten days have their own words: ついたち (1st), ふつか (2nd), みっか (3rd), よっか (4th), いつか (5th), むいか (6th), なのか (7th), ようか (8th), ここのか (9th) and とおか (10th). From the 11th on you just add にち to the number, as in じゅういちにち (11th), じゅうごにち (15th) and さんじゅうにち (30th).
texts.Seven later dates are special, and the b: Seven later dates are special, and the book stars them: じゅうよっか (14th), じゅうしちにち (17th), じゅうくにち (19th), はつか (20th), にじゅうよっか (24th), にじゅうしちにち (27th) and にじゅうくにち (29th). The 14th and 24th borrow よっか from the 4th. The 17th, 19th, 27th and 29th use しち and く instead of なな and きゅう. Ask with なんにち (what day of the month).
texts.4.5 Years and full dates: nen: 4.5 Years and full dates: ねん
texts.A year is the number plus nen. Say the n: A year is the number plus ねん. Say the number the way you learned in Chapter 3 and then add ねん: 2018 is にせんじゅうはちねん and 1995 is せんきゅうひゃくきゅうじゅうごねん. When the last digit is 4 it becomes よ: 2024 is にせんにじゅうよねん (not にじゅうよんねん). The digit 7 can be なな or しち, so 2017 is にせんじゅうななねん (にせん じゅうしちねん is also used). Ask with なんねん (what year).
texts.A full date goes from big to small: year: A full date goes from big to small: year, then month, then day. So January 6 is いちがつ むいか and January 9, 2017 is にせんじゅうななねん いちがつ ここのか. This is the same big to small order you used for the hour and the minutes.

texts.The words for days are irregular, so lea: The words for days are irregular, so learn them as a set: おととい (the day before yesterday), きのう (yesterday), きょう (today), あした (tomorrow), あさって (the day after tomorrow) and まいにち (every day).
texts.For a morning or a night, join the day w: For a morning or a night, join the day word to あさ (morning) or よる (night) with no: きのうの あさ is yesterday morning and あしたの よる is tomorrow night. A few have their own words: けさ (this morning), こんばん (tonight), ゆうべ (last night, the same as きのう の よる), まいあさ (every morning) and まいばん (every night). The word まい means every, and a まい word does not take no.
texts.Weeks and months follow one pattern. The: Weeks and months follow one pattern. The prefix せん means last, こん means this, らい means next, and さら means next next. Add a second せん to go one more step back, so せんせんしゅう is the week before last. Put each in front of しゅう (week) or げつ (month): せんしゅう, こんしゅう, らいしゅう, さらいしゅう and せんげつ, こんげつ, らいげつ, さらいげつ。
texts.Years are irregular, so learn them as a: Years are irregular, so learn them as a set: おととし (last last year), きょねん (last year), ことし (this year), らいねん (next year) and さらいねん (next next year). For every, use まい: まいしゅう (every week), まいつき or まいげつ (every month), まいとし or まいねん (every year).
texts.To attach one of these words to a day or: To attach one of these words to a day or a month, link them with no: らいしゅうの げつようび is next week Monday. A まい word does not take no, so every Monday is まいしゅう げつようび.
texts.4.8 A wa Time Expression desu: 4.8 A は Time Expression です
texts.A time expression can sit in a desu sent: A time expression can sit in a です sentence just like a noun. A は Time Expression です says that A is at, on or in that time, and you can turn it around: Time Expression は A です means the time is A. English needs a little word like at, on or in, but here Japanese needs no marker at all. You just put the time before です. This is ぶんけい 4.1 in your workbook.
texts.A can be an event, such as a class, a me: A can be an event, such as a class, a meeting, a holiday or a birthday. The time can be a clock time, a day of the week, a date, or any word from the last lessons, such as さらいげつ or まいしゅう きんようび。
texts.Add kara right after a time to say from: Add から right after a time to say from that time. The word から marks the starting point: くじ じゅうごふんから is from 9:15. It works with any time word, whether it is a clock time, a day, a month or a year. This is ぶんけい 4.2 in your workbook.
texts.Add made right after a time to say until: Add まで right after a time to say until or up to that time. The words から and まで often work as a pair, with Time から Time まで meaning from one time to another: ごご にじから ごじまで is from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. When you say from and until together, each marker sits right after its own time. This is ぶんけい 4.3 in your workbook.
texts.The word choudo means exactly. You can p: The word ちょうど means exactly. You can put it in front of the time or after it, so ちょうどさんじ and さんじ ちょうど both mean exactly 3 o'clock. It is mostly used with clock times, to say that it is neither a little before nor a little after. This is ぶんけい 4.4 in your workbook.
texts.Add goro right after a time to say aroun: Add ごろ right after a time to say around that time. The word ごろ goes with a point in time, such as 7 o'clock, the 10th or November. A length of time, such as three hours, uses ぐらい instead, and you will meet that in Chapter 5. The words ちょうど and ごろ are opposites: ちょうど says exactly and ごろ says roughly. This is ぶんけい 4.5 in your workbook.
texts.4.13 A wa Time Expression plus marker de: 4.13 A は Time Expression plus marker です
texts.You can put kara, made, goro or choudo w: You can put から, まで, ごろ or ちょうど with a time and then finish the sentence with です. The time plus its marker works like one noun, so the sentence shape is still A は (time plus marker) です. For example, クラスは さんじから ろくじまでです means The class is from 3 to 6 o'clock. The markers add clarity: から gives the start, まで gives the end, ごろ gives a rough time and ちょうど gives an exact one. This is ぶんけい 4.6 in your workbook.
texts.4.14 A wa itsu desu ka and the time ques: 4.14 A は いつですか and the time question words
texts.To ask when something is, say A wa itsu: To ask when something is, say A は いつですか. To ask about one part of a time, put なん (what) in front of its ending: なんじ (what time), なんぷん (what minute), なんにち (what day of the month), なんようび (what day of the week), なんがつ (what month) and なんねん (what year). The phrase いつごろ means around when.
texts.All of these can take a marker before de: All of these can take a marker before です か, so なんじ から です か asks from what time, and なんじ まで です か asks until what time. Add か at the end to make the question, and answer by putting the real time where the question word was. This is ぶんけい 4.7 in your workbook.
texts.Japan has four seasons, and the book fix: Japan has four seasons, and the book fixes them by month: はる (spring) is March to May, なつ (summer) is June to August, あき (autumn) is September to November and ふゆ (winter) is December to February. The general word for season is きせつ. The rainy season is つゆ.
texts.Seasons work in the same sentences as th: Seasons work in the same sentences as the other time words: にほんの ふゆは じゅうにがつからです says that winter in Japan starts in December.
texts.4.16 Time ni A ga arimasu (the marker ni: 4.16 Time に A が あります (the marker に)
texts.This extra lesson fills a gap. Exercise: This extra lesson fills a gap. Exercise V question 10 in the workbook asks a question with a marker that the Chapter 4 patterns do not teach: に. The marker に shows the time when something is held or exists, like on Sunday or at 3 p.m. The sentence uses the shape from Chapter 2, Place に A が あります, with a time in the に slot: Time に A が あります.
texts.Use this when something exists or happen: Use this when something exists or happens at that time, such as a class, a meeting or a party. The A は Time です sentences from this chapter do not need に, because です already says that A is at that time. Words like きょう, あした, きのう and まいにち do not take に.
texts.There is a meeting tomorrow (no ni after: There is a meeting tomorrow (no に after あした).
texts.big event, tournament (as in supo-tsu ta: big event, tournament (as in スポーツたいかい)
texts.The ending ji tells the hour, and fun or: The ending じ tells the hour, and fun or ぷん tells the minutes. さんじ is 3 o'clock, but さんぷん is 3 minutes.
texts.Say the hour first and the minutes after: Say the hour first and the minutes after it: くじ じゅうごふん is 9:15.
texts.The word han means half past, so juuniji: The word はん means half past, so じゅうにじ はん is 12:30. You can also say the full minutes, さんじゅっぷん.
texts.Only three hours are special: 4 o'clock: Only three hours are special: 4 o'clock is よじ, 7 o'clock is しちじ and 9 o'clock is くじ.
texts.Do not say yonji, nanaji or kyuuji. They: Do not say よんじ, ななじ or きゅうじ. They sound natural to a learner, but they are wrong.
texts.The other hours are plain: ichiji, niji,: The other hours are plain: いちじ, にじ, さんじ, ごじ, ろくじ, はちじ, じゅうじ, じゅういちじ and じゅうにじ。
texts.pun goes with 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10: ippu: ぷん goes with 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10: いっぷん, さんぷん, よんぷん, ろっぷん, はっぷん, じゅっぷん。
texts.fun goes with 2, 5, 7 and 9: nifun, gofu: fun goes with 2, 5, 7 and 9: にふん, ごふん, ななふん, きゅうふん。
texts.Bigger numbers follow the last digit: ju: Bigger numbers follow the last digit: じゅうごふん (15), にじゅういっぷん (21), よんじゅうごふん (45).
texts.Round tens take the squeezed sound: jupp: Round tens take the squeezed sound: じゅっぷん (10), にじゅっぷん (20), さんじゅっぷん (30).
texts.Gozen, gogo and han: ごぜん, ごご and はん
texts.gozen (a.m.) and gogo (p.m.) go in front: ごぜん (a.m.) and ごご (p.m.) go in front of the time, never after it: ごご しちじ is 7 p.m.
texts.han goes after the hour: gozen kuji han: はん goes after the hour: ごぜん くじ はん is 9:30 a.m.
texts.gozen and gogo name a.m. and p.m. The wo: ごぜん and ごご name a.m. and p.m. The words あさ, ひる and よる mean morning, noon and night.
texts.April is shigatsu, July is shichigatsu a: April is しがつ, July is しちがつ and September is くがつ.
texts.Do not say yongatsu, nanagatsu or kyuuga: Do not say よんがつ, なながつ or きゅうがつ。
texts.The other months are plain: ichigatsu, n: The other months are plain: いちがつ, にがつ, さんがつ, ごがつ, ろくがつ, はちがつ, じゅうがつ, じゅういちがつ, じゅうにがつ。
texts.The ending gatsu names a month on the ca: The ending がつ names a month on the calendar, like さんがつ (March). It does not count how many months pass.
texts.Dates that are not number plus nichi: Dates that are not number plus にち
texts.The 1st to the 10th are ten separate wor: The 1st to the 10th are ten separate words: ついたち, ふつか, みっか, よっか, いつか, むいか, なのか, ようか, ここのか, とおか。
texts.Seven later dates are special: juuyokka: Seven later dates are special: じゅうよっか (14th), じゅうしちにち (17th), じゅうくにち (19th), はつか (20th), にじゅうよっか (24th), にじゅうしちにち (27th), にじゅうくにち (29th).
texts.Every other date is the number plus nich: Every other date is the number plus にち: じゅういちにち (11th), じゅうごにち (15th), さんじゅうにち (30th).
よっか is the 4th, and ようか is the 8th. The 14th and 24th use よっか: じゅうよっか, にじゅうよっか。
texts.tooka is the 10th, and hatsuka is the 20: とおか is the 10th, and はつか is the 20th.
texts.futsuka is the 2nd, and hatsuka is the 2: ふつか is the 2nd, and はつか is the 20th. Both end in か, so check the start of the word.
むいか is the 6th and なのか is the 7th. Do not swap them.
texts.Itsu, itsuka and itsutsu: いつ, いつか and いつつ
texts.The word itsu means when. itsuka is the: The word いつ means when. いつか is the 5th day of the month. いつつ is five things.
texts.ikutsu asks how many things, ikura asks: いくつ asks how many things, いくら asks a price, どこ asks where, and いつ asks when.
texts.If the answer is a date such as gogatsu: If the answer is a date such as ごがつ いつか (May 5), the question was なんがつ なんにち.
texts.A year is the number plus nen, read like: A year is the number plus ねん, read like the big numbers from Chapter 3: せんきゅうひゃくきゅうじゅうごねん is 1995.
texts.When the last digit is 4, it becomes yo:: When the last digit is 4, it becomes よ: にじゅうよねん is the 24th year, so 2024 is にせんにじゅうよねん.
texts.When the last digit is 7, nana or shichi: When the last digit is 7, なな or しち both work: じゅうななねん and じゅうしちねん。
texts.The years in a full date go first: nisen: The years in a full date go first: にせんじゅうななねん いちがつ ここのか is January 9, 2017.
texts.Times go hour, then minutes: kuji juugof: Times go hour, then minutes: くじ じゅうごふん。
texts.A long time phrase goes from the biggest: A long time phrase goes from the biggest part to the smallest: らいしゅうの げつようび ごご さんじ。
texts.Kara, made and choudo: から, まで and ちょうど
texts.The word kara means from, and made means: The word から means from, and まで means until or up to. Each goes right after its own time.
ごご にじから ごじまで is from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. Put から after the first time and まで after the second.
texts.The word choudo means exactly. It goes b: The word ちょうど means exactly. It goes before the time or after it: ちょうどさんじ and さんじ ちょうど are the same.
texts.goro goes with a point in time: shichiji: ごろ goes with a point in time: しちじごろ is around 7 o'clock.
texts.gurai goes with an amount, such as a pri: ぐらい goes with an amount, such as a price (いくら ぐらい). You will use it for lengths of time in Chapter 5.
texts.choudo says exactly and goro says around: ちょうど says exactly and ごろ says around. Do not use both with the same time.
texts.Use no between a time word and a day or: Use no between a time word and a day or month: らいしゅうの げつようび, きょねんの ごがつ.
texts.Do not use no after mai: maishuu getsuyo: Do not use no after まい: まいしゅう げつようび is every Monday, not まいしゅう の げつようび.
texts.Use no between a day word and asa or yor: Use no between a day word and あさ or よる: きのうの あさ, あしたの よる.
texts.kesa, konban, yuube, maiasa and maiban s: けさ, こんばん, ゆうべ, まいあさ and まいばん stand alone, so there is no no.
texts.For weeks and months, sen is last, kon i: For weeks and months, せん is last, こん is this, らい is next and さら is next next: せんしゅう, こんしゅう, らいしゅう, さらいしゅう。
texts.A second sen goes one step further back:: A second せん goes one step further back: せんせんしゅう is last last week.
texts.Years are irregular: ototoshi, kyonen, k: Years are irregular: おととし, きょねん, ことし, らいねん, さらいねん. Last year is きょねん, not せんねん.
texts.Ototoi, kinou, ashita and asatte: おととい, きのう, あした and あさって
texts.ototoi is the day before yesterday, and: おととい is the day before yesterday, and きのう is yesterday. あした is tomorrow, and あさって is the day after tomorrow.
texts.kinou and kyou are long sounds: write th: きのう and きょう are long sounds: write the う at the end (きのう, きょう).
おととい and おととし start the same way. The first is two days back, and the second is two years back.
texts.kesa means this morning. kyou no asa is: けさ means this morning. きょう の あさ is not used.
texts.konban means tonight, and yuube means la: こんばん means tonight, and ゆうべ means last night. ゆうべ is the same as きのう の よる.
texts.The mai words mean every: maiasa (every: The まい words mean every: まいあさ (every morning), まいばん (every night), まいにち (every day).
texts.yoru and ban both mean night. ban shows: よる and ban both mean night. ban shows up inside words like こんばん and まいばん。
texts.nanji asks the hour, and nanpun asks the: なんじ asks the hour, and なんぷん asks the minutes. なんにち asks the date, and なんようび asks the day of the week.
texts.nangatsu asks the month, and nannen asks: なんがつ asks the month, and なんねん asks the year.
texts.The word itsu asks when in general, and: The word いつ asks when in general, and いつごろ asks around when.
texts.haru is spring, natsu is summer, aki is: はる is spring, なつ is summer, あき is autumn and ふゆ is winter. きせつ is the word for season.
texts.The book sets the seasons by month: haru: The book sets the seasons by month: はる is March to May, なつ is June to August, あき is September to November, ふゆ is December to February.
texts.Winter runs across the new year, so fuyu: Winter runs across the new year, so ふゆ goes from じゅうにがつ to にがつ.
texts.Four seasons is yottsu, using the genera: Four seasons is よっつ, using the general counter つ.
texts.In A wa Time desu there is no ni: kurasu: In A は Time です there is no に: クラス は すいようび です。
texts.With arimasu, use ni for the time someth: With あります, use に for the time something is held: にちようび に クラス が あります。
texts.Do not add ni after kinou, kyou, ashita: Do not add に after きのう, きょう, あした or まいにち. Do not add it after から, まで or ごろ。
texts.Class is jugyou or kurasu, and meeting i: Class is じゅぎょう or クラス, and meeting is かいぎ or ミーティング. Both of each pair are fine.
texts.First is mazu or hajime ni. Night is yor: First is まず or はじめに. Night is よる or ban.
texts.Yesterday night is yuube or kinou no yor: Yesterday night is ゆうべ or きのう の よる. Every month is まいつき or まいげつ。
texts.Yasumi, kyuukei and natsuyasumi: やすみ, きゅうけい and なつやすみ
texts.The word yasumi means a holiday or vacat: The word やすみ means a holiday or vacation. きゅうけい is a short break or rest.
texts.natsuyasumi is summer vacation, which is: なつやすみ is summer vacation, which is なつ plus やすみ.
A がっこう の やすみ is a school holiday. A きゅうけい is the break between classes.
texts.Write each time in romaji, hour first an: Write each time in romaji, hour first and then minutes. For example, 6:25 is ろくじ にじゅうごふん.
texts.Write each time in romaji with gozen or: Write each time in romaji with ごぜん or ごご in front. For example, 5:20 p.m. is ごご ごじ にじゅっぷん.
texts.Write each day in romaji. For example, M: Write each day in romaji. For example, Monday is げつようび.
texts.Write each month in romaji. For example,: Write each month in romaji. For example, August is はちがつ.
texts.Write each day of the month in romaji. F: Write each day of the month in romaji. For example, the 6th is むいか.
Write each day of the month in romaji. For example, the 13th is じゅうさんにち.
texts.Write each year in romaji. For example,: Write each year in romaji. For example, 2012 is にせん じゅうにねん.
texts.Write each date in romaji, from big to s: Write each date in romaji, from big to small: year, month, day. For example, February 14, 2020 is にせん にじゅうねん にがつ じゅうよっか.
texts.Write each word in romaji. For example,: Write each word in romaji. For example, this week is こんしゅう.
texts.Write each phrase in romaji. For example: Write each phrase in romaji. For example, this week Monday is こんしゅう の げつようび.

texts.yoji juugofun (よじ じゅうごふん): よじ じゅうごふん
texts.4 o'clock is the special reading yoji. 1: 4 o'clock is the special reading よじ. 15 minutes is じゅうごふん (it takes fun). The hour comes first.
texts.8 o'clock is hachiji. han means half pas: 8 o'clock is はちじ. はん means half past.
texts.juuichiji yonjuugofun (じゅういちじ よんじゅうごふん): じゅういちじ よんじゅうごふん
texts.11 o'clock is juuichiji. 45 minutes is y: 11 o'clock is じゅういちじ. 45 minutes is よんじゅうごふん (it takes fun). The hour comes first.
texts.kuji juugofun (くじ じゅうごふん): くじ じゅうごふん

texts.Chapter 4 gave you points in time: yoji: Chapter 4 gave you points in time: よじ is 4 o'clock, さんがつ is March and とおか is the 10th. Chapter 5 gives you lengths of time, which say how long something lasts: よじかん is 4 hours, さんかげつ is 3 months and とおかかん is 10 days. You use a length of time to talk about how long a class, a trip or a meeting takes.
texts.Most lengths of time are built by adding: Most lengths of time are built by adding an ending. Hours always end in じかん and weeks always end in しゅうかん, so those two endings never drop. For minutes, days, months and years you may add かん (span), but it is optional: さんぷん and さんぷんかん both mean 3 minutes. The book writes this as さんぷん(かん). Adding かん is a handy way to show that you mean a length and not a date, for example ふつかかん (2 days) next to ふつか (the 2nd).
texts.Months change their ending as well. Gats: Months change their ending as well. がつ names a month on the calendar (さんがつ is March), while かげつ counts months (さんかげつ is 3 months). Years work the same way: a year name like にせんにじゅうよねん (2024) is a point, and よねん is a length of 4 years.
texts.Minutes use the same endings as the cloc: Minutes use the same endings as the clock minutes in Chapter 4: ぷん for 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10, and fun for 2, 5, 7 and 9. The numbers 1, 6, 8 and 10 also squeeze the sound before ぷん: いっぷん, ろっぷん, はっぷん, じゅっぷん. The book lists よんふん next to よんぷん, and なんふん next to なんぷん, so both forms are fine. Bigger numbers follow their last digit: じゅうごふん is 15 minutes, にじゅっぷん is 20 minutes and よんじゅうごふん is 45 minutes. The かん after minutes is optional.
texts.Hours are the number plus jikan, and the: Hours are the number plus じかん, and the かん is part of the word, so it never drops: いちじかん is 1 hour and にじかん is 2 hours. The special clock readings carry over: 4 hours is よじかん (not よんじかん) and 9 hours is くじかん (not きゅうじかん). For 7 hours you have a choice, ななじかん or しちじかん, unlike the clock time, where only しちじ works. Put はん (half) after じかん for a half hour: いちじかんはん is 1 hour and a half. Large numbers just work: にじゅうじかん is 20 hours and ひゃくじかん is 100 hours.
texts.To ask, use nanpun (how many minutes) an: To ask, use なんぷん (how many minutes) and なんじかん (how many hours).
texts.One day is ichinichi. It is not the same: One day is いちにち. It is not the same word as ついたち, which is the 1st of the month. For 2 to 10 days, you use the same special words as the dates in Chapter 4: ふつか, みっか, よっか, いつか, むいか, なのか, ようか, ここのか and とおか. The かん after them is optional, but it helps to show that you mean a length: ふつか is the 2nd, and ふつかかん is 2 days. From 11 days on, the days are read like the dates from Chapter 4 too, for example じゅういちにち (11), じゅうよっか (14), じゅうごにち (15), はつか (20) and にじゅうはちにち (28). The book's table stops at 15 days, but its translation exercise asks for 28 days, so it is worth knowing that the pattern keeps going. Ask with なんにち (how many days). The book prints the question word as なんにちかん in one box.
texts.Weeks are the number plus shuukan, and t: Weeks are the number plus しゅうかん, and the かん always stays: いっしゅうかん is 1 week and にしゅうかん is 2 weeks. The numbers 1, 8 and 10 squeeze the sound: いっしゅうかん, はっしゅうかん, じゅっしゅうかん. Ask with なんしゅうかん (how many weeks).
texts.Months are the number plus kagetsu: nika: Months are the number plus かげつ: にかげつ is 2 months and さんかげつ is 3 months. The numbers 1, 6, 8 and 10 squeeze the sound: いっかげつ, ろっかげつ, はっかげつ and じゅっかげつ. For 8 months you can also say はちかげつ. Six months has a second name, はんとし (half a year), and one month can also be ひとつき. From 11 months, put じゅう in front: じゅういっかげつ is 11 months and じゅうにかげつ is 12 months. The かん is optional. Ask with なんかげつ (how many months).
texts.Years are the number plus nen, and the k: Years are the number plus ねん, and the かん is optional: いちねん, にねん, さんねん. Three numbers need care: 4 years is よねん (not よんねん), 7 years is ななねん or しちねん, and 9 years is きゅうねん. Do not mix these up with the year names from Chapter 4. にせん にじゅうよねん is the year 2024, and よねん is a length of 4 years. Ask with なんねん (how many years). The book prints the question word as なんねんかん in one box.
texts.5.5 A wa Span of Time desu (bunkei 5.1): 5.5 A は Span of Time です (ぶんけい 5.1)
texts.A length of time is a noun, so it can en: A length of time is a noun, so it can end a copula sentence just like the ones from Chapter 1. The pattern is A は Span of Time です, and it says that A lasts that long. A is the thing you are measuring, such as a class, a meeting, a trip or a holiday. Put は after A and です after the length of time. No other particle goes in between.
texts.Be careful to pick the right kind of wor: Be careful to pick the right kind of word. かいぎ は さんじ です uses a point in time, so the meeting is at 3 o'clock. かいぎ は さんじかん です uses a length of time, so the meeting lasts 3 hours. The last two rows of the table show the pair side by side.
5.6 Span of Time に Frequency (ぶんけい 5.2)
texts.To say how often something happens withi: To say how often something happens within a length of time, put に right after the length of time and then say the number of times with かい. いっしゅうかん に ごかい is five times a week. Read に here as per or in each: in one week, five times. The length is usually one unit (いちにち, いっしゅうかん, いっかげつ, いちねん), but it can be any length, such as よじかん に にかい (twice in four hours).
texts.The counter kai (times) comes from Chapt: The counter かい (times) comes from Chapter 3: いっかい、にかい、さんかい、よんかい, ごかい, ろっかい and so on. Ask how many times with なんかい. The whole phrase can finish a sentence with です, as in クラスは いっしゅうかんに にかいです (the class is twice a week). This に is different from the に of Chapter 4 that marks the time something happens, so do not mix them up.
texts.5.7 Span of Time gurai (bunkei 5.3): 5.7 Span of Time ぐらい (ぶんけい 5.3)
texts.Add gurai after a length of time to say: Add ぐらい after a length of time to say about or around: いちじかん ぐらい is about 1 hour. ぐらい goes right after the length, and it works with the かん form or the short form, so さんじゅっぷん ぐらい and さんじゅっぷんかん ぐらい are both fine. ぐらい also goes with amounts of money, which is why it appears in いくらぐらい later in this chapter.
texts.For a point in time you use goro from Ch: For a point in time you use ごろ from Chapter 4 instead. しちじ ごろ is around 7 o'clock, but ななじかん ぐらい is about 7 hours. A good way to remember it is ごろ for the clock and ぐらい for the length.
texts.5.8 Location kara and Location made (bun: 5.8 Location から and Location まで (ぶんけい 5.4)
texts.You already know kara (from) and made (u: You already know から (from) and まで (until, up to) after times. They also go after places: こうじょうから is from the factory and ぎんこうまで is up to the bank. から marks the starting point and まで marks the end point.
texts.To say how far a place is in time, put t: To say how far a place is in time, put the length of time right after the place: スーパーから ごふん is 5 minutes from the supermarket, and えきまで さんじゅっぷん is 30 minutes up to the station. You can also use both in one sentence: いえから がっこうまで じゅっぷんです says that it is 10 minutes from the house to school.
5.9 Span of Time まえ and すぎ (ぶんけい 5.5)
texts.Mae means before and sugi means after or: まえ means before and すぎ means after or past. They follow the time or the length of time directly, with nothing in between. After a clock time and a number of minutes, they say how far a moment is from the hour: いちじ ごふんまえ is 5 minutes before 1 o'clock, and にじ ごふんすぎ is 5 minutes past 2 o'clock. Say the hour first, then the minutes, then まえ or すぎ。
texts.After a length of time on its own, mae m: After a length of time on its own, まえ means ago or early: ごふん まえ is 5 minutes ago (or 5 minutes early), and いちじかんまえ is 1 hour ago. The book only shows すぎ with a clock time.
texts.5.10 Mode of transportation de (bunkei 5: 5.10 Mode of transportation で (ぶんけい 5.6)
texts.Put de after a vehicle to say how you go: Put で after a vehicle to say how you go: バス で is by bus and ひこうき で is by airplane. The table lists the vehicles. The one exception is あるいて (on foot, by walking). It already means by walking, so it takes no で: あるいて ごふんです is 5 minutes on foot.
texts.To mention two vehicles in one trip, joi: To mention two vehicles in one trip, join them with to: でんしゃ to バス で is by train and bus. The で phrase fits in front of a length of time or an amount: ちかてつで さんじゅっぷんです is 30 minutes by subway. The word で also means by or via, so a place can come before it, as in いえから じてんしゃで.
texts.5.11 A wa Interrogative desu ka (bunkei: 5.11 A は Interrogative です か (ぶんけい 5.7)
texts.To ask how long, use a question word mad: To ask how long, use a question word まで of なん plus the ending: なんぷん (how many minutes), なんじかん (hours), なんにち or なんにちかん (days), なんしゅうかん (weeks), なんかげつ (months) and なんねん or なんねんかん (years). The general question word is どのぐらい (how long), and it works for any length of time.
texts.Add ka at the end to turn the sentence i: Add か at the end to turn the sentence into a question: A は Interrogative です か. The answer uses the same sentence with a real length of time: A は Span of Time です. Pick the question word that matches the unit you expect in the answer. If you expect hours, ask with なんじかん.
texts.5.12 Span of Time kakarimasu and Cost ka: 5.12 Span of Time かかります and Cost かかります (ぶんけい 5.8)
texts.Kakarimasu is a verb. With a length of t: かかります is a verb. With a length of time it means takes, and with an amount of money it means costs. Put the length or the amount right before it: さんしゅうかん かかります is it takes 3 weeks, and せんえん かかります is it costs 1,000 yen. The thing that takes the time or the money can come first with は: しけんは さんじゅっぷんかかります is the exam takes 30 minutes. A place, a vehicle or both can come before the length, as in びょういんから ごふんかかります (it takes 5 minutes from the hospital) and バスで きゅうふんかかります (it takes 9 minutes by bus).
texts.Notice how this differs from A wa Span o: Notice how this differs from A は Span of Time です. です says that A is that long. かかります says that it takes that long. Both fit a class or a meeting. For money, use the number readings from Chapter 3, including the special ones: ろっぴゃく (600), はっぴゃく (800), さんぜん (3,000), and せん (1,000) on its own.
It costs 20,000 yen by しんかんせん.
texts.5.13 A wa donogurai kakarimasu ka (bunke: 5.13 A は どのぐらいかかりますか (ぶんけい 5.9)
texts.Donogurai means how long, and it asks ab: どのぐらい means how long, and it asks about a length of time. Put it in front of かかります か: どのぐらいかかりますか asks how long something takes. In A は どのぐらいかかりますか, A is the thing that takes the time, such as a meeting or a trip.
texts.You can use the other span question word: You can use the other span question words from lesson 5.11 in the same place, which gives Interrogative Noun かかります か: なんじかん かかります か asks how many hours it takes. どのぐらい is the open question, and words like なんじかん are more exact. Answer with a length of time and かかります, such as じゅうごふんかかります or いちじかん ぐらいかかります.
texts.5.14 A wa ikuragurai kakarimasu ka (bunk: 5.14 A は いくらぐらい かかります か (ぶんけい 5.10)
texts.To ask about money with kakarimasu, use: To ask about money with かかります, use いくら (how much) or いくらぐらい (about how much). いくらぐらい is the softer question, because it only asks for an estimate. The book's contents page lists the patterns up to ぶんけい 5.9, but the pages teach this tenth pattern, so it is included here.
texts.Donogurai asks about time and ikura or i: どのぐらい asks about time and いくら or いくらぐらい asks about money, even though both end in かかります か. The answer is an amount in yen followed by かかります: にまん えん かかります. Remember that the book sometimes writes いくらぐらい as two words, いくら ぐらい.
texts.How much will it cost by Shinkansen?: How much will it cost by しんかんせん?
texts.This last lesson is an extra that pulls: This last lesson is an extra that pulls the earlier ones into longer sentences, because the exercises need them. The usual order is the starting place with から, the end place with まで, the vehicle with で, and then the length of time or the cost with かかります. You can leave out any part you do not need.
texts.To answer How long does it take?, use a: To answer How long does it take?, use a length of time (and ぐらい if you are not sure): いえから えきまで バスで さんじゅっぷんかかります. To answer How much does it cost?, use an amount of money. The question words follow the same order: いえ から えきまで バスで どのぐらいかかりますか asks about time, and いえ から えきまで バスで いくら かかります か asks about money.
texts.It is about 3 hours from Osaka to Tokyo: It is about 3 hours from Osaka to Tokyo by しんかんせん.
texts.yoji is 4 o'clock, but yojikan is 4 hour: よじ is 4 o'clock, but よじかん is 4 hours. The ending かん turns a point into a length.
texts.sangatsu is March, but sankagetsu is 3 m: さんがつ is March, but さんかげつ is 3 months. しがつ is April, but よんかげつ is 4 months.
texts.tooka is the 10th, but tookakan is 10 da: とおか is the 10th, but とおかかん is 10 days.
texts.A year name like nisen nijuuyonen (2024): A year name like にせんにじゅうよねん (2024) is a point. よねん is a length of 4 years.
texts.kaigi wa sanji desu says the meeting is: かいぎは さんじです says the meeting is at 3 o'clock. かいぎは さんじかんです says it lasts 3 hours.
texts.Hours always keep jikan (ichijikan), and: Hours always keep じかん (いちじかん), and weeks always keep しゅうかん (いっしゅうかん).
texts.Minutes, days, months and years can drop: Minutes, days, months and years can drop かん. さんぷん, みっか, さんかげつ and さんねん are fine on their own.
texts.Add kan when you want to be clear that y: Add かん when you want to be clear that you mean a length. ふつか is the 2nd, and ふつかかん is 2 days.
texts.4 hours is yojikan and 9 hours is kujika: 4 hours is よじかん and 9 hours is くじかん, just like the clock times よじ and くじ. Do not say よんじかん or きゅうじかん。
7 hours can be ななじかん or しちじかん. The clock time 7 o'clock is only しちじ.
texts.ichijikan han is 1 hour and a half. ichi: いちじかんはん is 1 hour and a half. いちじ はん is 1:30 on the clock. はん goes at the end in both.
texts.Fun or pun in lengths: Fun or ぷん in lengths
The rules are the same as in Chapter 4. 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 10 take ぷん, and 2, 5, 7 and 9 take fun.
texts.1, 6, 8 and 10 also squeeze the sound: i: 1, 6, 8 and 10 also squeeze the sound: いっぷん, ろっぷん, はっぷん, じゅっぷん。
texts.Both yonpun and yonfun are fine for 4 mi: Both よんぷん and よんふん are fine for 4 minutes, and both なんぷん and なんふん are fine for how many minutes.
texts.Bigger numbers follow the last digit: ju: Bigger numbers follow the last digit: じゅうごふん (15), にじゅっぷん (20), よんじゅうごふん (45).
texts.futsuka is both the 2nd and 2 days. The: ふつか is both the 2nd and 2 days. The same goes for みっか, よっか, いつか and the other words up to とおか.
texts.One day is ichinichi, but the 1st is tsu: One day is いちにち, but the 1st is ついたち.
texts.From 11 days on, use the date words from: From 11 days on, use the date words from Chapter 4: じゅうよっか (14 days), はつか (20 days), にじゅうはちにち (28 days).
texts.Add kan to be sure the listener hears a: Add かん to be sure the listener hears a length: みっかかん is 3 days.
texts.itsuka is 5 days (or the 5th), and itsu: いつか is 5 days (or the 5th), and いつ means when. They look alike but they are different words.
texts.itsukakan is 5 days. itsu desu ka asks w: いつかかん is 5 days. いつですか asks when.
texts.The squeezed sound shows up for 1, 8 and: The squeezed sound shows up for 1, 8 and 10: いっしゅうかん, はっしゅうかん, じゅっしゅうかん. The other weeks do not squeeze: にしゅうかん, さんしゅうかん。
texts.One week is isshuukan, but this week is: One week is いっしゅうかん, but this week is こんしゅう from Chapter 4. Lengths use しゅうかん and names like this week use しゅう.
texts.gatsu names a month, and kagetsu counts: がつ names a month, and かげつ counts months. ろくがつ is June, but ろっかげつ is 6 months.
texts.ichigatsu is January, but ikkagetsu is 1: いちがつ is January, but いっかげつ is 1 month.
texts.hantoshi (half a year) means the same as: はんとし (half a year) means the same as ろっかげつ.
texts.1, 6, 8 and 10 squeeze the sound: ikkage: 1, 6, 8 and 10 squeeze the sound: いっかげつ, ろっかげつ, はっかげつ, じゅっかげつ。
texts.4 years is yonen, not yonnen. 7 years is: 4 years is よねん, not よんねん. 7 years is ななねん or しちねん. 9 years is きゅうねん.
texts.A year name from Chapter 4 says which ye: A year name from Chapter 4 says which year, and a length says how many years. にせんにじゅうよねん is the year 2024, but よねん is 4 years.
texts.gurai goes with a length: ichijikan gura: ぐらい goes with a length: いちじかん ぐらい is about 1 hour. It also goes with money: いくらぐらい。
texts.Do not say shichiji gurai or ichijikan g: Do not say しちじ ぐらい or いちじかん ごろ。
texts.Ni after a length or after a time: に after a length or after a time
texts.isshuukan ni nikai uses ni to mean per o: いっしゅうかん に にかい uses に to mean per or in each. It is followed by a number of times.
texts.nichiyoubi ni kurasu ga arimasu uses ni: にちようび に クラス が あります uses に to say when something happens.
texts.kinou, kyou, ashita and mainichi take no: きのう, きょう, あした and まいにち take no に at all.
texts.Kai for times and kai for floors: かい for times and かい for floors
texts.Both words are read kai, but the floor f: Both words are read かい, but the floor forms differ from the times forms. 3 times is さんかい, but the 3rd floor is さんがい.
texts.2 times and the 2nd floor are the same w: 2 times and the 2nd floor are the same word, にかい. Context tells you which one.
texts.Kara and made with places: から and まで with places
texts.kara marks the starting place and made m: から marks the starting place and まで marks the end place. えき から is from the station, and えき まで is up to the station.
texts.The length of time comes right after the: The length of time comes right after the place: えきまで さんじゅっぷん is 30 minutes up to the station.
texts.With times, kara and made work the same: With times, から and まで work the same way: ごご にじから ごじまで.
texts.Mae, made and sugi: まえ, まで and すぎ
まえ means before, and まで means until. They sound alike, so check the meaning.
texts.mae also means in front of, as in eki no: まえ also means in front of, as in えき の まえ from Chapter 2. After a time it means before.
texts.sugi means after or past: niji gofun sug: すぎ means after or past: にじ ごふんすぎ is 5 minutes past 2.
まえ and すぎ come after the whole time. Say いちじ ごふんまえ, not ごふん まえ いちじ.
texts.Mae with a time and mae with a length: まえ with a time and まえ with a length
texts.ichiji gofun mae is 5 minutes before 1 o: いちじ ごふんまえ is 5 minutes before 1 o'clock. It names a moment.
texts.gofun mae on its own is 5 minutes ago, o: ごふん まえ on its own is 5 minutes ago, or 5 minutes early.
texts.Put de after a vehicle: basu de is by bu: Put で after a vehicle: バス で is by bus, and ひこうき で is by airplane.
texts.aruite already means on foot, so it take: あるいて already means on foot, so it takes no で.
texts.To name two vehicles, join them with to:: To name two vehicles, join them with to: でんしゃ to バス で is by train and bus.
texts.Kakarimasu: time or money: かかります: time or money
texts.kakarimasu works for both time and money: かかります works for both time and money: いちじかん かかります takes 1 hour, and せんえん かかります costs 1,000 yen.
texts.kurasu wa yojikan desu says the class is: クラスは よじかんです says the class is 4 hours. クラス は よじかん かかります says the class takes 4 hours.
texts.The question tells you which one is mean: The question tells you which one is meant. どのぐらい asks about time, and いくら asks about money.
texts.Donogurai, ikura and ikuragurai: どのぐらい, いくら and いくらぐらい
texts.donogurai asks how long. ikura asks how: どのぐらい asks how long. いくら asks how much, and いくらぐらい asks around how much.
texts.nanjikan asks for hours only, but donogu: なんじかん asks for hours only, but どのぐらい can be answered with any length.
texts.ikura also asks a price in Chapter 3: ki: いくら also asks a price in Chapter 3: きっぷ は いくら です か。
texts.Pick the question word by the unit you w: Pick the question word by the unit you want back: なんぷん, なんじかん, なんにち, なんしゅうかん, なんかげつ, なんねん。
texts.nanji asks the time on the clock, but na: なんじ asks the time on the clock, but なんじかん asks how many hours.
texts.nangatsu asks which month, but nankagets: なんがつ asks which month, but なんかげつ asks how many months.
texts.Money amounts with kakarimasu: Money amounts with かかります
texts.1,000 yen is sen en, not ichisen en. 3,0: 1,000 yen is せん えん, not いちせん えん. 3,000 yen is さんぜん えん and 8,000 yen is はっせん えん.
texts.600 yen is roppyaku en and 800 yen is ha: 600 yen is ろっぴゃく えん and 800 yen is はっぴゃく えん.
texts.20,000 yen is ni man en, as in Chapter 3: 20,000 yen is にまん えん, as in Chapter 3.
texts.Oufuku and katamichi: おうふく and かたみち
texts.oufuku is a roundtrip, and katamichi is: おうふく is a roundtrip, and かたみち is one way.
texts.gakusei is the general word for a studen: がくせい is the general word for a student.
texts.seito is a pupil in a class, and ryuugak: せいと is a pupil in a class, and りゅうがくせい is a student studying abroad.
texts.kurasumeito is a classmate, and menba- i: クラスメイト is a classmate, and メンバー is a member of a group.
texts.takushi-, menba-, guru-pu, tore-ningu an: タクシー, メンバー, グループ, トレーニング and オートバイ use a hyphen for the long sound.
texts.Hiragana words double the vowel instead:: Hiragana words double the vowel instead: ひこうき, りゅうがくせい, しゅくだい。
texts.o-tobai or baiku is a motorcycle. jidous: オートバイ or バイク is a motorcycle. じどうしゃ or くるま is a car.
はっかげつ or はちかげつ is 8 months. ななじかん or しちじかん is 7 hours.
texts.yonpun or yonfun is 4 minutes. rokkagets: よんぷん or よんふん is 4 minutes. ろっかげつ or はんとし is 6 months.
texts.Yasumi, hiruyasumi and kyuukei: やすみ, ひるやすみ and きゅうけい
texts.yasumi is a holiday or vacation. hiruyas: やすみ is a holiday or vacation. ひるやすみ is a lunch break, from ひる (noon) and やすみ。
texts.kyuukei is a short break, such as the on: きゅうけい is a short break, such as the one between classes.
texts.This is the drill from the workbook (pag: This is the drill from the workbook (page 74). Write each length of time in Japanese. The book's example is 5 hours, which is ごじかん.

texts.1 week: ichishuukan or isshuukan?: 1 week: いちしゅうかん or いっしゅうかん？
texts.8 weeks: hachishuukan or hasshuukan?: 8 weeks: はちしゅうかん or はっしゅうかん？
texts.6 months: rokukagetsu or rokkagetsu?: 6 months: ろくかげつ or ろっかげつ？
texts.4 years: yonnen or yonen?: 4 years: よんねん or よねん？
texts.9 years: kuunen or kyuunen?: 9 years: くうねん or きゅうねん？

texts.1 day: tsuitachi or ichinichi?: 1 day: ついたち or いちにち？

texts.Part N: Before and after: mae and sugi: Part N: Before and after: まえ and すぎ

texts.kaigi wa ____ desu ka. (Answer: sanjuppu: かいぎ は ____ です か。 (Answer: さんじゅっぷん です。)
texts.kurasu wa ____ desu ka. (Answer: gojikan: クラス は ____ です か。 (Answer: ごじかん です。)
texts.tore-ningu wa ____ desu ka. (Answer: mik: トレーニング は ____ です か。 (Answer: みっかかん です。)
texts.zemi wa ____ desu ka. (Answer: nishuukan: ゼミ は ____ です か。 (Answer: にしゅうかん です。)
texts.tore-ningu wa ____ desu ka. (Answer: yon: トレーニング は ____ です か。 (Answer: よんかげつ です。)
texts.daigaku wa ____ desu ka. (Answer: yonenk: だいがく は ____ です か。 (Answer: よねんかんです.)
texts.kurasu wa isshuukan ni ____ desu ka. (An: クラス は いっしゅうかん に ____ です か。 (Answer: にかい です。)
texts.yasumi wa ____ desu ka. (Answer: nanokak: やすみ は ____ です か。 (Answer: なのかかん です。)

texts.kaigi wa ____ kakarimasu ka. (Answer: ic: かいぎ は ____ かかります か。 (Answer: いちじかん かかります。)
texts.oufuku wa ____ kakarimasu ka. (Answer: s: おうふく は ____ かかります か。 (Answer: さんぜん えん かかります。)
texts.shinkansen de ____ kakarimasu ka. (Answe: しんかんせん で ____ かかります か。 (Answer: さんじかん ぐらい かかります。)

texts.How much does it cost by Shinkansen?: How much does it cost by しんかんせん?
texts.One minute is ippun. After 1, pun gets a: One minute is いっぷん. After 1, ぷん gets a squeezed sound.
Three takes ぷん: さんぷん。
texts.yonpun / yonfun (よんぷん / よんふん): よんぷん / よんふん
texts.Four takes pun, and the book also lists: Four takes ぷん, and the book also lists よんふん. The かん after minutes is optional.
texts.Six takes pun with a squeezed sound: rop: Six takes ぷん with a squeezed sound: ろっぷん。
texts.Eight takes pun with a squeezed sound: h: Eight takes ぷん with a squeezed sound: はっぷん。
texts.Ten takes pun with a squeezed sound: jup: Ten takes ぷん with a squeezed sound: じゅっぷん。
じゅう (10) plus にふん (2). Two takes fun.
texts.ni juu (20) plus the squeezed pun: nijup: にじゅう (20) plus the squeezed ぷん: にじゅっぷん。
texts.san juu (30) plus the squeezed pun: sanj: さんじゅう (30) plus the squeezed ぷん: さんじゅっぷん。
texts.yon juu (40) plus gofun (5). Five takes: よんじゅう (40) plus ごふん (5). Five takes fun.
texts.nanpun / nanfun (なんぷん / なんふん): なんぷん / なんふん
texts.nan plus pun or fun. The book accepts bo: なん plus ぷん or fun. The book accepts both.
texts.The number plus jikan. The kan is part o: The number plus じかん. The かん is part of the word for hours.
The number plus じかん: にじかん。
Special reading: よじかん, not よんじかん.
The number plus じかん: ろくじかん。
texts.nanajikan / shichijikan (ななじかん / しちじかん): ななじかん / しちじかん
texts.Both are fine for lengths. The clock tim: Both are fine for lengths. The clock time 7 o'clock is only しちじ.
Special reading: くじかん, not きゅうじかん.
texts.Ten is juu, so juu plus jikan is juujika: Ten is じゅう, so じゅう plus じかん is じゅうじかん.
にじゅう (20) plus じかん.
ひゃく (100) plus じかん.
はん (half) goes after じかん.
にじかん (2 hours) plus はん (half).
texts.One day is ichinichi. The 1st of the mon: One day is いちにち. The 1st of the month is a different word, ついたち.
texts.2 days uses the same word as the date: f: 2 days uses the same word as the date: ふつか. Adding かん (ふつかかん) is also fine.
texts.3 days uses the same word as the date: m: 3 days uses the same word as the date: みっか. Adding かん (みっかかん) is also fine.
texts.5 days uses the same word as the date: i: 5 days uses the same word as the date: いつか. Adding かん (いつかかん) is also fine.
texts.6 days uses the same word as the date: m: 6 days uses the same word as the date: むいか. Adding かん (むいかかん) is also fine.
texts.8 days uses the same word as the date: y: 8 days uses the same word as the date: ようか. Adding かん (ようかかん) is also fine.
texts.10 days uses the same word as the date:: 10 days uses the same word as the date: とおか. Adding かん (とおかかん) is also fine.
texts.The number plus nichi: juugonichi. It is: The number plus にち: じゅうごにち. It is read like the 15th. かん is optional.
texts.The 20th has its own word, hatsuka, and: The 20th has its own word, はつか, and it is used for 20 days too.
texts.ni juu (20) plus hachi (8) plus nichi: n: にじゅう (20) plus はち (8) plus にち: にじゅうはちにち. It is read like the 28th.
texts.nannichi / nannichikan (なんにち / なんにちかん): なんにち / なんにちかん
